version.changelog:
agent-memory-system v1.0.0

- Initial release of the long-term memory system for OpenClaw Agent.
- Features temperature-based memory management (hot/warm/cold) with automatic archiving of data older than 30 days.
- Includes nightly reflection with health monitoring and periodic memory cleanup.
- Enables extraction of reusable skills from lessons learned.
- Provides directory templates and scripts for installation, cron automation, and troubleshooting.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions align with its stated purpose (local long‑term memory management): it manipulates files under a workspace, archives old notes, generates reports, and can scaffold extracted skills — there are no hidden network calls or secret-collection behaviors, but the scripts do modify user files and suggest cron persistence, so review/backup before enabling is recommended.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (agent long‑term memory, temperature model, GC, nightly reflection, skill extraction) match the provided scripts and templates. All required actions (moving old markdown to .archive, generating reports, creating reflection files, scaffolding a skill from a lesson) are coherent with the purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts operate on a local workspace (default $HOME/.openclaw/workspace). They create/modify files and directories (memory/, .archive/, skills/), run simple shell utilities (find, mv, grep, sed), and suggest adding cron entries. The extract-skill.sh will modify lesson files' frontmatter (adds status/skill-path via sed) — this is within the skill's remit but is an intrusive file-write action the user should expect and review.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present (instruction-only). No downloads or external package installs are performed by the skill itself. Scripts are local shell scripts; nothing is fetched from remote URLs during normal operation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no credentials or environment variables. It respects an optional WORKSPACE env var but defaults to $HOME/.openclaw/workspace. Because it writes and moves files under that workspace (including modifying lesson files and creating skill packages), granting it access to the workspace is necessary but gives it file‑modification capability — this is proportionate to purpose but worth attention.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not set to always:true and is user-invocable. However SKILL.md instructs users to add cron jobs to run GC and nightly reflection automatically, which creates persistent scheduled behavior on the host. The scripts themselves do not register cron entries automatically — the user must add them.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: manage a local markdown-based memory workspace, archive old notes, generate reports, create daily reflection files, and scaffold skills from lessons. Points to consider before installing or enabling automated execution: 1) Review the three scripts (extract-skill.sh, memory-gc.sh, nightly-reflection.sh) yourself — they modify and move files under $HOME/.openclaw/workspace by default (extract-skill.sh will update lesson frontmatter and write new skill directories). 2) Make backups of your workspace (or test in a copy) before running, especially before running extract-skill.sh which alters lesson files in-place. 3) memory-gc.sh supports --dry-run — use it first to see what would be archived. 4) Be aware the SKILL.md suggests adding cron jobs; only add them if you want automatic scheduled runs. 5) On macOS, sed -i usage in scripts may behave differently (BSD sed requires an argument after -i); test scripts on your platform. 6) No network calls or credential exfiltration were found, but if you change WORKSPACE to a different path the scripts will operate there — avoid pointing WORKSPACE at sensitive directories. If you want, run the scripts manually first and inspect the generated changes before enabling cron automation.
